les: Te klein om te sien, groot genoeg om siek te maak
kaps_punt: Die verband tussen kieme en siektes en die rol van Louis Pasteur.

items.bewering: Mense kon sien dat siekte van mens tot mens versprei, maar nie wat dit oordra nie.
items.bron: World History Encyclopedia, 'Religious Responses to the Black Death' (worldhistory.org/article/1541): people understood the plague passed between people yet had no cause for it; miasma/germ-theory histories (Wikipedia 'Miasma theory', 'Germ theory of disease') note the idea of contagion long predated any knowledge of microbes as the carrier. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Daarom het hulle siekte dikwels aan slegte lug of aan 'n straf toegeskryf.
items.bron: Miasma theory ('bad air' from rotting matter as the accepted cause of disease through the Middle Ages and into 19th-century cholera explanations): Wikipedia 'Miasma theory' and mirrors; divine punishment for sin as the dominant popular explanation of plague: World History Encyclopedia, 'Religious Responses to the Black Death'. 'dikwels' is accurate; neither was universal. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Baie mense het ook geglo dat klein lewende dinge vanself uit dooie stof ontstaan.
items.bron: OpenStax Microbiology 3.1 'Spontaneous Generation' (openstax.org/books/microbiology/pages/3-1-spontaneous-generation): the long-held theory that life arises from non-living matter, which Pasteur's experiments disproved. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Louis Pasteur was 'n Franse wetenskaplike wat in die 1860's hierdie geloof getoets het.
items.bron: Institut Pasteur, 'Louis Pasteur: a universal legacy' (pasteur.fr/en/node/19656): 'the most famous French scientist', a chemist; began the spontaneous-generation research in 1858. Wellcome Collection record: lecture 'Sur les corpuscules organises qui existent dans l'atmosphere', Societe chimique de Paris, 19 May 1861; published Annales de chimie et de physique 1862; Alhumbert Prize 1862 and the 'omne vivum ex vivo' lecture 1864 (OpenStax 3.1). The work began in 1858-59 but its experiments, publication and prize fall in the early 1860s, so 'in die 1860's' holds as written. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Hy het vloeistof in glasflesse gegiet. Daarna het hy die vloeistof in die flesse gekook om die klein lewende dinge daarin dood te maak.
items.bron: OpenStax Microbiology 3.1: Pasteur boiled broth in the flasks to sterilise it; Memorial University biology page 'Pasteur Swan-Neck' (mun.ca/biology/scarr/4270_Pasteur_experiment.html). Full check, this round.

items.bewering: By party flesse kon die lug met sy stoffies by die vloeistof kom. Daardie vloeistof het troebel geword en vrot geraak.
items.bron: OpenStax Microbiology 3.1 and its figure: when the neck is broken, microorganisms enter and the broth becomes cloudy; Institut Pasteur: microbes proliferated once the broth came into contact with dust particles. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: By ander flesse was die lang nek gebuig soos 'n swaan s'n.
items.bron: The comparison maps on shape only, which is what the flask is named for ('swan-neck' flasks: OpenStax 3.1, mun.ca). No further inference a learner would draw from a swan's neck leads anywhere false; the mechanism is stated separately in the next sentence. Mapping checked, this round.

items.bewering: Die nek het lug ingelaat en die stoffies vasgevang. In dié flesse het dieselfde vloeistof skoon gebly.
items.bron: OpenStax Microbiology 3.1: air could move in and out, but airborne microorganisms were caught in the bends of the neck ('Dust, particles, and bacteria settle in the bend of the flask'); the broth in intact flasks stayed sterile. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Die bederf het dus van buite gekom en nie uit die vloeistof self nie.
items.bron: OpenStax Microbiology 3.1 and Britannica 'Louis Pasteur: Spontaneous generation' (search summary): the experiment showed microbes in the broth came from airborne particles, not from the broth arising spontaneously. The lesson claims only this experiment's conclusion, not that spontaneous generation is impossible in general, which is the correct scope. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Die flesse het oor bederf gegaan en nie oor siekte nie. Pasteur en ander wetenskaplikes het van daar verder gedink.
items.blok: Van vrot kos na 'n siek mens
items.bron: OpenStax 3.1 (the flask experiments concern broth contamination); Newcastle University 'Health and the People: germ theory' and 'Robert Koch' (healthandthepeople.ncl.ac.uk/germ-theory): the link to specific diseases was built afterwards by Pasteur and others, Koch above all (anthrax 1876, tuberculosis 1882). Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Klein lewende dinge kan kos en wyn laat bederf.
items.blok: Van vrot kos na 'n siek mens
items.bron: Institut Pasteur (pasteur.fr/en/node/19656): Napoleon III asked Pasteur to study wine diseases in 1863; his 1865 patent: 'Wine does not spoil if the microbes are killed beforehand.' Science History Institute profile of Pasteur. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Sulke dinge kan dan ook in 'n mens se liggaam kom en hom siek maak. Dit is die verband tussen kieme en siekte.
items.blok: Van vrot kos na 'n siek mens
items.bron: KidsHealth (Nemours), 'Germs: Bacteria, Viruses, Fungi, and Protozoa' (kidshealth.org/en/teens/care-about-germs.html): germs are microscopic organisms that can cause disease; Newcastle University 'germ theory'. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Kieme is baie klein lewende dinge wat 'n mens siek kan maak. 'n Enkele kiem is te klein om met die blote oog te sien.
items.blok: Van vrot kos na 'n siek mens
items.bron: KidsHealth (Nemours), 'Germs': germs are microscopic bacteria, viruses, fungi and protozoa that can cause disease. 'kan' correctly avoids saying every small living thing is harmful. MSU Extension notes mould growths can be seen without a microscope, but a growth is many organisms; the lesson says 'n enkele kiem', which holds. Viruses are germs whose status as living things is debated in science; the standard child-health definition calls germs organisms, so the sentence is the accepted school-level reading rather than an error. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Daardie verband het 'n nuwe manier gebied om siekte te voorkom. 'n Mens kon kieme weghou of hulle doodmaak.
items.blok: Van vrot kos na 'n siek mens
items.bron: World History Encyclopedia 'Germ Theory' (worldhistory.org/Germ_Theory) and Newcastle University 'germ theory': germ theory led to antiseptic and hygiene practice (killing germs) and to keeping them out; pasteurisation (FDA) kills them by heat. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Op 'n houer vars melk in jou eie huis staan dikwels dat die melk gepasteuriseer is.
items.bron: South African sources: Checkers listing for Clover Fresh Full Cream Milk 2L (checkers.co.za) describes it as fresh pasteurised milk; Clover's own product pages are titled 'Clover Ultra Pasteurised Full Cream Milk' / 'Ultra Pasteurised Low Fat Milk' (clover.co.za); SA dairy regulations (R260 of 2015 / R1510 of 2019, Agricultural Product Standards Act) use 'pasteurised' and 'ultra pasteurised' as categories of milk. I did not see a carton image, so the claim rests on product names and listings; 'dikwels' keeps it safely inside that. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Daardie melk is warm gemaak om die skadelike kieme daarin dood te maak. Daarna hou die melk langer, en is dit veiliger om te drink.
items.bron: US FDA consumer page on raw milk (fda.gov/food/resourcesforyou/consumers/ucm079516.htm): pasteurisation kills harmful germs by heating milk to a set temperature for a set time; CDC and FDA call raw milk unsafe. Shelf life: pasteurisation also destroys many spoilage organisms, so refrigerated pasteurised milk keeps longer (Wikipedia 'Pasteurization', Scientific American 'What is pasteurization'). Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Hierdie metode is na Pasteur vernoem.
items.bron: Institut Pasteur (pasteur.fr/en/node/19656): 1865 patent for preserving wine by heating; Smithsonian Magazine 'When Food Changed History: Louis Pasteur': the process was named pasteurisation in his honour. Note the lesson does not say Pasteur pasteurised milk himself (that was proposed by Soxhlet in 1886), which is correct. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Pasteur het nie kieme ontdek nie. Ander mense het hulle meer as honderd jaar voor hom onder 'n mikroskoop gesien.
items.bron: Priority claim. Antonie van Leeuwenhoek saw microbes ('animalcules') through his own microscopes in 1674-1676 and reported them to the Royal Society in a letter of 9 October 1676 (Wikipedia 'Antonie van Leeuwenhoek'; Smithsonian Ocean ocean.si.edu; Hektoen International). Pasteur was born in 1822 and did this work from 1858 (Institut Pasteur), roughly 180 years later, so 'meer as honderd jaar' holds. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Hy het ook nie alleen bewys dat kieme siekte veroorsaak nie. Sy proewe het gewys waar bederf vandaan kom. Daarmee het hy die idee versterk dat kieme siekte veroorsaak.
items.bron: Priority claim. Newcastle University 'Health and the People: Robert Koch' and 'germ theory' (healthandthepeople.ncl.ac.uk): Koch's anthrax work (1876) was the first rigorous proof that one microbe causes one disease, and he identified the tuberculosis bacillus (1882); Pasteur made germ theory persuasive. OpenStax 3.1 for what the flask experiments showed. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Hy het later entstowwe teen siektes van diere en teen hondsdolheid gemaak.
items.bron: Institut Pasteur (pasteur.fr/en/node/19656): fowl cholera 1879, anthrax for sheep at Pouilly-le-Fort June 1881, rabies treatment of Joseph Meister 6 July 1885; Britannica 'Louis Pasteur: Vaccine development'. 'later' is correct (after the 1860s flask work). Nature (d42859-020-00008-5) records that credit for the anthrax method is disputed with Toussaint, but the lesson names no single animal vaccine and fowl cholera is uncontested, so the sentence holds. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: Daardie entstowwe het gewys dat 'n mens die verband kon gebruik om siekte te voorkom. Die verband was dus nie net 'n verklaring vir siekte nie.
items.bron: Institut Pasteur: attenuated microbes protected fowl and sheep, and by March 1886 350 people had been treated against rabies; Science History Institute profile of Pasteur. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: kieme: Baie klein lewende dinge wat 'n mens siek kan maak. 'n Enkele kiem is te klein om met die blote oog te sien.
items.bron: Same as the identical study-block sentence: KidsHealth (Nemours) 'Germs'. The entry reads true on its own. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: bakterie: Een soort baie klein lewende ding; sommige bakterieë is kieme wat siekte veroorsaak.
items.bron: KidsHealth (Nemours) 'Germs': bacteria are one-celled organisms; some are helpful and others cause infections. 'sommige' is the right quantifier. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: pasteurisering: 'n Manier waarop melk of 'n ander vloeistof warm gemaak word om die skadelike kieme daarin dood te maak.
items.bron: FDA (heating milk to kill harmful germs); Institut Pasteur (the process began with wine, so 'of 'n ander vloeistof' is correct). Full check, this round.

items.bewering: entstof: 'n Middel wat 'n liggaam help om 'n bepaalde siekte later te weerstaan.
items.bron: WHO Q&A 'Vaccines and immunization: What is vaccination?' (who.int): a vaccine produces an immune response without causing illness and protects against a disease, often for years; CDC vaccine glossary: a preparation that stimulates the body's immune response against disease. Full check, this round.

items.bewering: hondsdolheid: 'n Gevaarlike siekte wat meestal deur die byt van 'n siek dier oorgedra word.
items.bron: WHO fact sheet 'Rabies' (who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/rabies): spreads via saliva, usually through bites and scratches; dogs responsible in up to 99% of human cases; virtually always fatal once symptoms appear. 'meestal' correctly leaves room for scratches and mucosal contact. Full check, this round.

opsomming: Every claim in all ten blocks was checked against the web this round and every one holds, including the dating of the flask experiments to the 1860s, the 'more than a hundred years' gap to Leeuwenhoek, and the careful wording of what Pasteur did not do; the lesson has no 'first'-type superlatives, and its one comparison (the swan's neck) maps on shape only.
